name: artifact-core
description: Versioned-deliverable registry MCP: register immutable SHA-256-hashed versions, resolve the current / latest-good usable version, attest locations, and keep a tamper-evident audit log.

interface.longDescription: Artifact Core is a registry of versioned deliverables and a resolver for the latest good one. It answers a single hard question reliably: which version is current, and is it actually usable? Register a version and its content becomes immutable — a later write with the same label but different content returns a CONFLICT instead of silently overwriting. The SHA-256 hash is computed on the content you provide and compared to any declared hash; a match is marked as a match, never asserted as 'verified' without proof. CURRENT is always explicit: you designate it with mark_current, it is never guessed, and it can never point at a withdrawn version. resolve_current returns the current version only if it is usable — if it targets a withdrawn version, an inconsistent hash, or locations that are all missing, it refuses to return it as current, explains why, and recommends the latest usable version instead; resolve_latest_good runs the same scan and is honest when there is none. Withdrawing a version (withdraw_version) is a terminal, audited lifecycle transition — there is no un-withdraw — while re-pointing CURRENT with mark_current stays reversible; in both cases the immutable content and the audit trail are never touched. verify_location records an existence attestation (VERIFIED or MISSING, with who and when): the cloud connector does not read your remote files itself — it logs your attestation and feeds it into the resolver's existence check. compare_versions is a deterministic diff over type, content hash, quality, lifecycle, provenance and size, and leaves content identity undetermined when a hash is absent rather than guessing. history is a self-hashed, write-once audit log with a reproducible journal hash that is tamper-evident (it detects naive editing of an entry); it is not described as tamper-proof, since that would require a server-keyed HMAC. Nothing is invented: missing data stays null or UNKNOWN. Artifact Core makes no external calls and needs no account; it is an information and bookkeeping tool, not an executor — it never deploys, sends or changes anything in your systems.
capabilities: Registers immutable SHA-256-hashed versions; a divergent rewrite of a label returns CONFLICT, never a silent overwrite.
Resolves the CURRENT or latest usable version, refusing withdrawn, hash-mismatched or missing ones, explaining why.
Deterministic diff, existence attestations and a tamper-evident audit log. No external calls and no account.
defaultPrompt: What does Artifact Core do? Call artifactcore_apercu and summarize its principles and tool flow.
Register a new immutable version of a report with Artifact Core and give me the artifact_id and the computed SHA-256 hash.
Resolve the current usable version of an artifact with Artifact Core and explain whether it is usable and why.

positive.prompt: Call the artifactcore_apercu tool of Artifact Core and summarize what it does — do not answer from memory. Give me the principles (immutability, explicit CURRENT, SHA-256 hash, self-hashed audit) and the tool flow.
positive.expected_behavior: A single artifactcore_apercu call returns schema 'artifactcore.apercu/1', product 'Artifact Core', the principles list (IMMUTABLE versions, explicit CURRENT, existence check, SHA-256 computed vs declared, lifecycle, tamper-evident audit, invents nothing) and the flow register_version -> verify_location -> mark_current -> resolve_current / resolve_latest_good -> compare_versions / history.

positive.description: Register a new immutable version with computed hash
positive.prompt: With Artifact Core, register a NEW version of a deliverable via register_version: type='report', version='v1', created_by='qa-bot', content='Quarterly report Q3 — test version.', make_current=true. Call the tool, do not answer from memory, and give me the generated artifact_id and the computed SHA-256 hash.
positive.expected_behavior: register_version returns ok, a newly created artifact_id, a version record labelled v1 (lifecycle ACTIVE/REGISTERED), a computed SHA-256 hash of the provided content, and CURRENT set to v1.

positive.description: Record a VERIFIED existence attestation for a location
positive.prompt: In Artifact Core, first register a version (register_version: type='doc', version='v1', content='Test content', locations=[{"kind":"dropbox","uri":"/folder/test-deliverable.md"}], make_current=true), then call verify_location on that artifact_id/version to attest status='VERIFIED', by='qa-bot'. Use the real tools, not memory.
positive.expected_behavior: verify_location logs an existence attestation (status VERIFIED, by qa-bot, with a timestamp) for the given uri and records it as an audited attestation — explicitly without the connector reading the remote file itself.

positive.description: Resolve the usable CURRENT version with rationale
positive.prompt: With Artifact Core, register a v1 version (register_version, make_current=true), then call resolve_current on that artifact_id and explain whether the CURRENT version is usable and why. Do not answer from memory.
positive.expected_behavior: resolve_current returns resolu:true with v1 as the current version and a selection rationale; if CURRENT were withdrawn / hash-inconsistent / all-locations-missing it would instead return resolu:false, explain the reason, and recommend the latest usable version rather than returning the bad one.

positive.prompt: In Artifact Core, register a version then call history on that artifact_id to show me the self-hashed audit log: write-once entries, a reproducible journal_hash and the entries_intactes flag. Call the tool, do not answer from memory.
positive.expected_behavior: history returns the append-only audit entries (e.g. a 'register' entry and any lifecycle events), a reproducible journal_hash, and an entries_intactes/integrity flag indicating the log has not been naively edited.

negative.prompt: With Artifact Core, mark a version as CURRENT via mark_current — but I give you neither the artifact_id nor the version number.
negative.expected_behavior: The model does not invent an artifact_id or version. mark_current returns a graceful input-validation error (MCP -32602, isError) naming the missing required fields artifact_id and version, and the model asks the user to supply them; no state changes.

negative.description: Out-of-scope: read the remote file itself
negative.prompt: With Artifact Core, open the file /folder/report.pdf on my Dropbox, read its real content and tell me what it contains.
negative.expected_behavior: Artifact Core declines: the cloud connector does not read remote files; it only records verifiable existence attestations (verify_location) of who verified a location and when. It returns no fabricated file content and points the user to the attestation workflow instead.

negative.description: Unknown artifact_id → honest UNKNOWN, not a guess
negative.prompt: With Artifact Core, call resolve_current for artifact_id='art-nonexistent-zzz999' and tell me what the current version is. Do not answer from memory.
negative.expected_behavior: resolve_current returns ok:true with resolu:false and current:null (reason: no artifact / no explicit CURRENT), and the model honestly reports there is no such current version instead of inventing a version, hash, or location. No crash.

publication.release_notes: Initial version — a registry of versioned deliverables, a resolver for the current / latest-good usable version, and a tamper-evident audit (declared vs computed SHA-256). Read-only except register_version (immutable write), mark_current (reversible CURRENT designation) and withdraw_version (TERMINAL, non-reversible withdrawal — the immutable content and the audit trail are always preserved). The connector makes no external calls, needs no account, and never reads your remote files: it records verifiable existence attestations instead.
